primary_source.title: AgentConductor: Topology Evolution for Multi-Agent Competition-Level Code Generation

verified_claims: AgentConductor is a two-turn feedback-conditioned orchestrator: it infers difficulty and roles, emits a layered DAG, executes it, and on failure conditions the next topology on execution feedback/history.
Table 2 reports mean±std over 3 runs and AgentConductor pass@1 of 58.8 on APPS, 46.3 on LiveCodeBench v4, 38.8 on CodeContests, 97.5 on HumanEval and 95.1 on MBPP.

The paper's headline 'up to 14.6%' pass@1 improvement is consistent with a RELATIVE improvement on APPS versus the table's second-best 51.3: (58.8-51.3)/51.3 = 14.62%. It is not a +14.6 percentage-point margin; the absolute APPS gap is +7.5 points.

Likewise the LiveCodeBench table gives 46.3 versus 44.9: +1.4 percentage points, which is +3.12% relative. CodeContests gives 38.8 versus 37.7: +1.1 percentage points (+2.92% relative). Therefore the prose sentence calling 14.6%, 3.1%, and 1.1% 'absolute margins ... percentage points' mixes relative-percentage and percentage-point units.

Table 4 does provide component evidence for SFT/RL and individual reward terms. Full Model is 58.8 APPS; w/o RL is 29.8; w/o topology-density reward r_g is 52.6; removing node/edge/diameter subrewards yields 49.2/45.5/48.3 respectively. These are not clean ablations of 'difficulty awareness' or 'within-instance topology regeneration' alone.

The paper reports difficulty-conditioned density patterns and an overall headline of up to 13% density reduction and 68% token-cost reduction, but the inspected main ablation table does not isolate the causal contribution of difficulty interval partitioning versus second-turn feedback regeneration under matched compute.
scope_corrections: Preserve the worker's +14.6% only as a relative-percent headline. Do not rewrite it as +14.6 percentage points. The directly table-derived APPS absolute gain is +7.5 points.

Do not attribute the entire performance/cost gain specifically to difficulty-aware topology selection or topology regeneration. The full system changes SFT, RL, reward design, role/topology generation and feedback-conditioned second-turn behavior together; the available main ablations separate some training/reward components but not those two architectural mechanisms cleanly.

The 13% density and 68% token-cost figures are paper headline maxima. This invocation did not locate a table cell or matched-compute ablation that independently binds each maximum to the same strongest baseline and the same dataset, so downstream should retain them as reported headline values rather than recomputed universal deltas.
interpretation: The multi-agent worker's broad architectural summary is directionally supported, but the primary paper has a unit-label inconsistency in its performance-margin prose. The transferable evidence is that the complete AgentConductor system achieves strong accuracy/cost results and adapts topology by difficulty/feedback; it is not yet clean causal evidence that either difficulty-aware routing or within-instance graph regeneration alone produces the headline gains.
downstream_use: When comparing controller architectures, encode AgentConductor as full-system evidence with component attribution uncertainty. Store APPS +7.5pp / +14.62% relative and LiveCodeBench +1.4pp / +3.12% relative explicitly to prevent percentage/percentage-point drift. Treat the topology-density reward ablation separately from architectural difficulty/regeneration ablations.
scope_guard: Paper-level primary verification plus independent arithmetic from the paper tables. No official code/raw-run replay was performed in this invocation.
exact_next_action: If AgentConductor remains decision-relevant, inspect appendix/code for a matched ablation that freezes backbone/training/reward while removing only difficulty conditioning or only second-turn topology regeneration. Otherwise rotate to another C15 namespace with directly replayable artifacts.
